01 • Why this pilot

Start small enough to learn. Build strong enough to scale.

The purpose is not simply to install five labs. It is to demonstrate a repeatable way of bringing practical technology learning into government schools.

Students should move beyond only consuming technology to building, testing, debugging and applying it.

The proposed pilot brings infrastructure, grade-wise learning, teacher enablement, digital support and project-based activities together as one programme.

Five schools create a controlled environment to observe what works, refine implementation and generate evidence before considering wider adoption.

Hands-on learning is the operating principle — students build with guidance, tools and real hardware.
02 • What changes in a school

From a room with equipment to a functioning learning ecosystem.

The lab is designed around repeated classroom use, not one-time demonstrations.

Proposed school model

  • Dedicated AI Robotics & Innovation learning space
  • AI, robotics, coding, electronics, IoT and prototyping
  • Grade-wise structured activities for Grades 1–10
  • Teacher manuals, student manuals and digital learning support
  • Hands-on projects, demonstrations and showcases
  • Teacher and student enablement
  • Utilisation and learning evidence
  • A model that can be refined before scale
03 • Inside the lab

Five connected capability zones.

Different tools, one learning loop: understand → build → test → improve. The visual below combines real implementation photographs with one illustrative proposed lab configuration.

AI & Robotics

Robots, sensors, AI concepts, computer vision, autonomous systems and applied robotics projects.

Build • Program • Test

Electronics & IoT

Circuits, microcontrollers, sensors, automation and connected physical systems.

Connect • Measure • Automate

3D Prototyping

Digital-to-physical making through CAD, 3D printing, iteration and functional prototypes.

Design • Print • Refine

Coding & Computing

Block-based logic, programming, computational thinking and software connected to physical systems.

Code • Debug • Apply

Maker + Science

Mechanical construction, experimentation, science applications, design thinking and project development.

Question • Make • Discover

Project & Showcase

A visible space for prototypes, demonstrations, exhibitions and student-led problem solving.

Demonstrate • Explain • Improve

05 • Grades 1–10

A progression from curiosity to capability.

The complexity grows with the learner — from making and observation to engineering, coding and applied AI.

GRADES 1–2

Discover

Curiosity, simple mechanisms, patterns, observation and guided making.

Explore → Build
GRADES 3–5

Explore

Simple robotics, electronics, coding logic, experiments and model building.

Build → Test
GRADES 6–8

Apply

Sensors, automation, programming, IoT, 3D prototyping and engineering projects.

Test → Solve
GRADES 9–10

Innovate

AI, computer vision, advanced robotics, integrated projects and real-world problem solving.

Solve → Innovate

07 • Who benefits

One programme. Different stakeholder outcomes.

The value of the pilot is different for the student, teacher, school and government — but all four are connected.

Students

Move from passive learning toward building, experimentation and applied problem solving.

  • AI & robotics exposure
  • Coding and electronics
  • 3D prototyping
  • Creativity and problem solving
  • Projects and showcases

Teachers

Gain a structured environment, resources and support to facilitate hands-on learning.

  • Teacher enablement
  • Ready learning resources
  • Practical activity guidance
  • Project facilitation
  • Confidence with new technologies

Schools & Government

Create a visible, measurable and potentially replicable model for future-ready education.

  • Technology infrastructure
  • Utilisation evidence
  • Student project evidence
  • Teacher capacity building
  • Scale decision framework
08 • Implementation

Six steps from school readiness to measurable impact.

Implementation is treated as a programme, not an installation event.

01 • ASSESS

Understand

Review school space, infrastructure, timetable, teacher availability and implementation conditions.

02 • DESIGN

Plan

Configure the lab, learning journey, equipment, resources and operating model.

03 • SETUP

Install

Deploy infrastructure, tools, technology, content and digital support.

04 • ENABLE

Activate

Orient teachers and begin structured student activities and project work.

05 • MEASURE

Evidence

Track participation, utilisation, projects, skills and programme observations.

06 • REFINE

Decide

Use evidence to improve the model and inform any future scale decision.

09 • Implementation roadmap

A practical operating sequence.

Each stage has a clear purpose and handoff so the programme can be managed across five schools.

01

School selection

Confirm participating schools and implementation readiness.

02

Assessment

Review space, electricity, connectivity, storage and timetable.

03

Lab setup

Install infrastructure, equipment, tools and learning resources.

04

Teacher enablement

Orient teachers and establish the operating rhythm.

05

Student activation

Run grade-wise activities, projects and practical sessions.

06

Review

Document evidence, showcase work and refine the model.

10 • What we measure

Measure activity first. Then outcomes.

The pilot should generate evidence that helps decision-makers understand whether the model is working and what needs improvement.

Implementation evidence

  • Lab readiness and utilisation
  • Teacher participation and enablement
  • Sessions and activities conducted
  • Equipment and resource utilisation
  • School-level implementation observations

Learning & outcome evidence

  • Student participation
  • Projects and prototypes created
  • Skills demonstrated through activities
  • Student showcases and exhibitions
  • Qualitative feedback and improvement opportunities
11 • Vision

What success looks like beyond the pilot.

Short term

Make the five pilot schools active, visible learning environments.

  • Labs are operational and used
  • Teachers are enabled
  • Students build regularly
  • Projects are documented
  • Evidence is available for review

Long term

Use a validated model to support wider adoption across government schools.

  • Replicable lab architecture
  • Grade-wise learning framework
  • Teacher enablement model
  • Project and showcase ecosystem
  • Evidence-led scale decisions
12 • The proposal

What we are asking Thane to consider.

Consider a five-school proposed pilot to test an integrated AI Robotics & Innovation learning model in government schools.

  • Identify five suitable government schools for the proposed pilot
  • Enable school-level assessment and implementation planning
  • Review the proposed lab and learning ecosystem
  • Support access to teachers, timetable and school infrastructure
  • Evaluate evidence at the end of the pilot before any scale decision
Representative visual: the intended shift from classroom instruction to hands-on technology learning.
13 • Final message

Five schools can become the evidence base for a larger model.

The proposed Thane pilot is an opportunity to establish, activate, measure and refine a practical technology-learning ecosystem before considering wider implementation.

Proposed principle: infrastructure + curriculum + teacher enablement + student projects + evidence → informed scale.
